- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.25) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.75) and price is trending up, model frequently overfits upward momentum; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or mean.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.25–0.75), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast toward 3–5 day moving average if price deviates >1.5σ from recent range.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is weak or volatile.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast to reflect sentiment-driven sell-off.
